statement.p: (a) Find a vector parallel to the line of intersection of the planes 5 x - y + 3 z = -1 and -5 x - y - 3 z = 3.
(b) Show that the point \left(-1,-1,1\right) lies on both planes. Then find a vector parametric equation for the line of intersection.

static.solution:
(a) Normal vectors to the two planes are \vec n_1 = 5\vec i - \vec j + 3 \vec k \quad \hbox{ and } \quad \vec n_2 = - 5\vec i - \vec j - 3 \vec k. The vector \vec n_1\times\vec n_2 is perpendicular to both planes and parallel to the line of intersection: \vec n_1\times\vec n_2 = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} \vec i \amp \vec j \amp \vec k\\ 5 \amp -1 \amp 3\\ -5 \amp -1 \amp -3 \end{array} \right| = 6\,\mathit{\vec i}-10\,\mathit{\vec k}.
(b) To check that the point \left(-1,-1,1\right) lies on the planes, substitute into each equation. 5 x - y + 3 z = (5)(-1) + (-1)(-1) + (3)(1) = -1, and -5 x - y - 3 z = (-5)(-1) + (-1)(-1) + (-3)(1) = 3. Thus, the point lies on both planes. Then a vector parametric equation of the line is \vec r(t) = \left(6t-1\right)\,\mathit{\vec i}-\,\mathit{\vec j}+\left(1-10t\right)\,\mathit{\vec k}.
